newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foreign units seen underpinning NAB growth.
newsitem.headline: Foreign units seen underpinning NAB growth.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd will become increasingly dependent on its overseas operations to continue its run of record breaking results as the local market comes under further pressure, analysts said on Thursday.
NAB shares fell nearly two percent despite the bank's announcement of a 14.1 percent rise in first half net profit to A$1.14 billion, within market expectations.

Analysts attributed the fall to profit-taking after the strong rise in bank shares over the past three months combined with the general tightness in the Australian banking market which was likely to mean limited profit growth.
"On (the) outlook, NAB will out-perform given the diversification of its asset mix," said a Melbourne analyst.
"Its overseas operations will make it achieve superior growth to assist some of its domestic businesses," he said.
NAB's operations in the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand and Asia contributed to 37 percent of the first half profit, compared with about 29 percent a year ago.

"All the banks are doing it very tough in Australia at the moment," said the analyst, who asked not to be identified. Profit from NAB's local operations rose 1.4 percent in the half, while all overseas units had double-digit growth.
NAB's rival Westpac Banking Corp reported a fall in first half profit from its Australian operations on Wednesday, although it recorded a 12.9 percent hike in its overall profit.

Analysts said NAB's first half profit was a good result and there was no need to change their 1996/97 full year forecasts, which range from A$2.23 billion to A$2.47 billion for the 12 months to September 30, 1997.
Although the results from NAB's domestic operations were relatively flat, the A$721 million net profit posted was still seen as a good achievement, analysts said.

"In Australia they have done pretty well in offsetting margin pressure through higher volumes and therefore profitability has been sustained," said a Sydney-based analyst, who also did not want to be named.
NAB hit a record high of A$18.55 before the result announcement but by 3.05 p.m. (0505 GMT), NAB shares were 27 cents lower at A$18.07 along with other bank majors.

A Melbourne fund manager said: "Banks have been loved by the share market for a long time because of their superior profit growth, but after today's result and Westpac's, it is time for investors to question where do bank profits go from here."
